output.answer: Representative class actions against Synchrony Bank include Taylor et al. v. Synchrony Bank et al., alleging it clawed back military interest-rate benefits through higher interest and fees after active duty; on August 4, 2026, the court affirmed arbitration of Taylor’s and Hawkins’s claims and stayed those proceedings. Habel v. Synchrony Bank, filed June 1, 2026, alleges prerecorded debt-collection calls continued after consent was revoked, violating the federal Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA) and California debt-collection law. S.G. v. Synchrony Bank challenged CareCredit interest rates under New York usury law; the court ordered arbitration and stayed the case on March 25, 2026. Earlier robocall class actions include Lucas v. Synchrony Bank ($2.6 million settlement finally approved April 25, 2023) and consolidated Neal/Campbell litigation ($2.9 million settlement agreement), involving calls about accounts that did not belong to recipients.
caveats: This is a representative list, not an exhaustive litigation history; it excludes securities litigation solely against parent Synchrony Financial and government enforcement proceedings.
The allegations in Taylor, Habel and S.G. are not findings of liability, and arbitration stays do not establish wrongdoing. Synchrony did not admit wrongdoing in the cited TCPA settlements.

Later developments may have occurred: the opened Habel docket showed only early June 2026 activity. A final-approval order for the Neal/Campbell settlement was not verified; the opened report described an agreement and a hearing scheduled for March 15, 2021.

key_facts.fact: The amended Taylor/Hawkins class complaint names Synchrony Bank and alleges that interest and fee increases after active duty improperly recaptured military interest-rate benefits.
The court affirmed the order compelling Taylor’s and Hawkins’s claims to arbitration and stayed proceedings concerning those claims.
Habel v. Synchrony Bank was filed in the Southern District of California.
Habel seeks a nationwide class over alleged prerecorded calls after consent was revoked and alleges violations of the TCPA and California’s Rosenthal Fair Debt Collection Practices Act.
The court’s report describes S.G.’s putative CareCredit class action, filed August 19, 2024, alleging violations of New York usury law.
The court granted Synchrony Bank’s motion to compel arbitration and stayed S.G.’s case pending arbitration.

The court finally approved the $2.6 million Lucas settlement concerning prerecorded calls about accounts not belonging to recipients, certified the settlement class and dismissed the action with prejudice.

A published report describes a $2.9 million settlement agreement resolving consolidated Curtis Neal and Roy Campbell TCPA claims against Synchrony Bank over calls about other people’s accounts; the report’s publication date was not available.
